title: Assays for studying normal versus suppressive ERAD-associated retrotranslocation pathways in yeast
author: Bhaduri, Neal

steps.title: Design primers and amplify KanMx
steps.instruction: Use forward primer A and reverse primer B (Figure 1, key resources table) to PCR‑amplify the KanMx gene from plasmid pSN26, adding 50 bp homologous arms flanking the Dfm1 coding region.

steps.title: Perform PCR with Phusion polymerase
steps.instruction: Set up a 50 µL PCR using Phusion polymerase; run 25–30 cycles with annealing at 59 °C for 40 s and extension at 72 °C for 1 min.

steps.title: Check PCR product on gel
steps.instruction: Load the amplified product on a 1 % agarose gel, run, and visualise the ~1.5 kb band with a ChemiDoc system.

steps.title: Store or use PCR product directly
steps.instruction: PCR reactions may be stored at –20 °C for later use; otherwise, use the 50 µL reaction directly for yeast transformation (no cleanup required).

steps.title: Transform yeast with PCR cassette
steps.instruction: Transform competent yeast cells with the 50 µL PCR product to replace the Dfm1 ORF with the KanMx cassette via homologous recombination.

steps.title: Select and verify dfm1Δ knockouts
steps.instruction: Plate transformants on G418‑containing media, then confirm correct integration by diagnostic PCR using primers C/D (≈150 bp product) and E/F (≈200 bp product).

steps.title: Optional alternative markers
steps.instruction: If desired, repeat the above using NatMx (plasmid pSN27) or HphMx (plasmid pSN28) with the same primers.

steps.title: Prepare cultures for flow analysis
steps.instruction: Thaw, inoculate, and passage dfm1Δ‑null yeast containing GALpr‑Hmg2‑GFP as described (e.g., up to passage P11). Include biological triplicates and technical triplicates for each strain.

substeps.instruction: Set up the following controls: non‑induced (glucose), degraded Hmg2 (WT + GALpr‑Hmg2‑GFP, galactose), stabilized Hmg2 (cdc48‑2 + GALpr‑Hmg2‑GFP, galactose), Sample 1 (P0 dfm1Δ + GALpr‑Hmg2‑GFP, non‑passaged), Sample 2 (passaged dfm1Δ + GALpr‑Hmg2‑GFP, suppressed).

steps.title: Induce GFP substrate expression
steps.instruction: Grow cultures to OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.4, then add galactose and incubate for at least 2 h to induce GALpr‑Hmg2‑GFP.

steps.title: Collect cells for cytometry
steps.instruction: Take 300 µL of each culture (including controls) and keep suspended in minimal media for immediate analysis.

steps.title: Configure flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Set the BD Biosciences FACS Calibur (or BD Accuri) to run limits of 10 000 events and medium fluidics flow rate for yeast.

steps.title: Acquire data and gate populations
steps.instruction: Run each 300 µL sample on the collector; acquire a density plot (SSC vs FSC) and a histogram (Cell Count vs 530 nm filter for GFP FITC‑A). Draw Gate 1 (red) around intact cells and exclude Gate 2 (purple) representing ruptured cells.

steps.title: Determine mean fluorescence
steps.instruction: From the gated histogram, record the mean fluorescence of the intact cell population (e.g., P0 ≈ 50 000, suppressed P11 ≈ 20 000). Repeat for all passages, ensuring cells are in log phase (OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.4) to avoid debris.
